task1: well to moderately formed tubular glandular architectures, infiltrative tumor margins extending irregularly into the stroma, and a prominent desmoplastic stromal reaction with scattered areas of luminal necrotic debris.
task2: complex, irregularly shaped glandular structures invading the bowel wall, extensive regions of luminal dirty necrosis, and a dense, fibrous desmoplastic stroma lacking significant peritumoral lymphoid aggregates.

task1: prominent mucinous differentiation characterized by large extracellular mucin pools, frequent serrated or cribriform glandular growth patterns, and expansile or pushing tumor margins with variable stromal cellularity.
task2: solid or medullary tumor growth patterns lacking well-defined glands, distinct pushing tumor margins, and a prominent peritumoral Crohn's-like lymphoid reaction featuring conspicuous lymphoid follicles with germinal centers.

task1: pseudostratified columnar tumor cells with elongated hyperchromatic nuclei, distinct cell borders with apical mucin depletion, and prominent intraluminal granular necrotic debris (dirty necrosis) within the glandular structures.
task2: closely packed, irregular glands lined by pleomorphic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, frequent mitotic figures, distinct nuclear molding, and a notable absence of prominent intraepithelial lymphocytes.

task1: atypical epithelial cells frequently floating in abundant extracellular mucin, vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli, loss of normal glandular architecture, and occasional presence of focal signet-ring cell morphology.
task2: poorly differentiated tumor cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli arranged in solid sheets, heavily interspersed with numerous tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and variable focal regions of mucinous differentiation.
